thesis: Amazon.com is a global retailer and technology platform. **[Fact]** Customers pay for physical and digital goods (North America and International stores), cloud infrastructure (AWS), advertising, and third-party seller services. **[Fact]** Cash to shareholders comes from operating cash flow after capital spending on logistics and data centers, not from a single product line. **[Fact]** FY2025 net sales were **$716.9 billion** (+12%); Q1 2026 net sales **$181.5 billion** (+17%). **[Fact]** AWS is the profit engine: Q1 2026 AWS sales **$37.6 billion** (+28%) with segment operating income margin **37.7%**. **[Inference]** Reported free cash flow is temporarily depressed by AI-related capital spending while operating cash flow remains large.
why_market_wrong: There is **no clear dated mispricing signal** (HK predictive attribute: **none**). **[Inference]** The market prices Amazon as a growth compounder with embedded artificial intelligence optionality, not as a distressed asset. **[Inference]** The debate is whether **normalized owner cash flow** after capital spending (not trailing twelve-month free cash flow of **$1.2 billion**) supports the multiple at today's price. Return is **franchise earnings power at price**, contingent on capital spending moderating toward a **~$90 billion** sustainable run rate versus trailing purchases of **$147.3 billion**.
